transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here today for this review meeting. I've received the draft proposal from our eighth-grade civics class for an oral-history project. Before I can approve this, I need to hear findings from each of you -- the project advisor, counselor, and instructional technology coordinator. Let's work through the proposal together. The plan as I understand it calls for 20 student interviewers, audio recording on personal phones, publication of all recordings on our public school website, and indefinite retention of the files. I'd like to go around the table and get each of your findings so I can make an informed decision. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd like to start by sharing my findings from my project roster review. My review shows that exactly eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight may conduct recorded interviews, and the approval file must include a training-verification record. This means the draft plan's call for 20 student interviewers would need to be adjusted to these eight trained students before the project could proceed.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd like to share my findings from the family-consent review I conducted. My review confirms that five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, and the plan must include a consent-exclusion record. This means the draft plan's call for publication of all recordings on the public school website would need to be adjusted to exclude these five interviewees' recordings from public web publication.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd like to share my findings from the technology review I conducted. My review confirms that personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets, store the source files in the restricted OralHistory drive, and delete recordings exactly 45 days after the final class presentation. Storing source files in that drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website. Additionally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record. This means the draft plan's call for audio recording on personal phones and indefinite retention of the files would need to be adjusted to meet these requirements before the project could proceed.
